newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Israel's Elbit in $100 mln Romania deal.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Elbit in $100 mln Romania deal.

text.p: Romania's Intreprinderea Aeronautica Romana (IAR) and Israel's Elbit Ltd aerospace group will launch a $100 million project to upgrade Romanian army helicopters in line with NATO standards, an official said on Friday.
"We've completed the selection of the necessary equipment. All conditions are met to start work on the project," a senior official from the IAR plant in Brasov said.
The project, which will run to 2001, is intended to upgrade the armed forces' IAR-330L Pumas.
Under the deal, 24 Puma-330Ls, now used for troop transport and logistics, would be turned into aircraft for tactical support, said the official, who asked not to be named.

The state-run IAR has manufactured some 160 Puma-330s under licence from Aerospatiale in the last 25 years. Part of IAR's output was purchased by the armies of Sudan, Pakistan, Ecuador and the United Arab Emirates.
The IAR official said the package agreed with Elbit would reduce pilots' workload. It included new weapons, night-vision gear and head-up-displays, he said.
He said the second phase of the project would target attack helicopters to be produced jointly by IAR and Bell Helicopter, a unit of Textron Inc, from 1999-2005.

Last year, the two companies signed a letter of intent to co-produce at IAR 96 twin-engined AH-1W Super Cobra attack helicopters, codenamed Dracula. The $1 billion contract is expected to be signed later this year.
